> Omi is a simple desktop companion. Functionality includes date/time, timer, stopwatch, countdown, and audio visualizer which responds to the sounds in your working space (e.g. typing). It can also display humidity and temperature of your working space. It's a device that is for the most part single-purpose, meaning it doesn't occupy more of your attention than it needs.

# using kicad for the first time
it's my first hardware project, so i followed the tutorial up until the beginning part of the push buttons.
i think it's not as hard as i though.

##what did i get done
- figured out how to install symbol libraries (thanks yt)
- found out i didnt install the power libraries? (idk if that's what they're called)

luckily the installs all went smoothly, but i had to search up how to do some of the things not explicitly stated in the guide. like crossing out the unused pins, and drawing the wire and box.

# finished schematic and pcb :3
1.5 h - finished wiring the rest of the schematic (everything aside from the esp32)

1h - researching how the footprint editor on the schematic worked and adding the footprints to the parts

2.5 h - trying to figure out
	1) why i couldn't add the footprint
	2) how to get to footprint libraries (i was in schematic editor which only had preferences > symbol libraries, but i saw many references online going to preferences > footprint libraries. i eventually realized it wasn't in the schematic editor, it was in the pcb editor | i also realized that i could have just gone into the main kicad launch window thing and went prefernces > footprint libraries)
	3) how to install lookout (for desktop recording sessions via lapse, to record kicad activity). uh, i don't think it's possible on arch (??), one of the packages is like missing or not available (l
1h - doing the custom star shaped boundary on the edge cuts layer  - i couldn't close the loop at first because i kept placing the last point on the wrong place, and then escaping or pressing enter to finish the shape, but then the entire freaking thing disappeared... i ended up just using slanted lines, and spent some time adjusting the shape until it looked pretty good to me.

4 h - routing pcb :)
	- maybe it was because it was my first time, but i ran in to lots of weird things i didn't know. so i had to ask for help in slack a ton, lmao.
	- also, i got like way more traces than in the guide, i don't know if anything wrong , but i'm pretty sure i didn't, because if i only routed some of the traces as shown in the guide, i would have lots of unconnected stuff
	- i got 28 pcb violations in DRC :skul:
		- i lwk just deleted everything (in the pcb editor) and redid some parts in the schematic, then reloaded the schematic into the pcb editor
	- my friend told me some tips to keep in mind when doing the pcb, so i went in and changed some stuff based on his feedback

1h - adding silkscreen images :3
- had to look up how to add the images, at first i had symbols in schematic but then i couldn't assign footprints to them, also, they were really big because i didn't make them smaller in the image converter lol
- hack club logo and sillicates(silly cats) :)
